## The Busyhead Project

In 2023, Noah Kahan launched **The Busyhead Project**, a mental health initiative named after his 2019
debut album *Busyhead*. The project reflects Kahan's own openness about his experiences with anxiety and
depression, which he has discussed candidly in interviews and woven throughout his songwriting.

Through the initiative, Kahan has directed proceeds from portions of his tour and merchandise sales toward
mental health organizations, aiming to reduce stigma and expand access to mental health resources —
particularly for young people and touring musicians, a population that faces unique pressures on the road.

## Advocacy Through Music

Kahan's lyrics frequently touch on mental health, family strain, and the difficulty of asking for help,
themes that resonated strongly with fans navigating similar struggles. Songs like "Growing Sideways" and
"False Confidence" directly reference his experience with therapy and anxiety, helping normalize those
conversations for a mainstream pop audience.

::: {.callout-quote}
"I wanted to make something that gave back to the community that helped raise me, and to a cause that's
been such a huge part of my life and my music." — on the founding of The Busyhead Project
:::

## Getting Involved

Fans interested in supporting mental health causes connected to Kahan's advocacy can look for
Busyhead Project fundraising campaigns tied to his tours, or support mental health organizations directly
in their own communities.

::: {.callout-important}
This page summarizes publicly reported philanthropic activity for informational purposes. For current
campaign details or ways to donate, refer to official Noah Kahan or Busyhead Project channels.
:::
